workflow_title: Clinical decision support (CDS) selection, implementation, and lifecycle monitoring for health IT-enabled clinical workflows
occupation_scope: Clinical informaticist; Chief medical informatics officer; Clinical decision support analyst; Informatics nurse
workflow_summary: An institution reviews a clinical problem (care gap, alert fatigue, safety event), selects or designs a CDS intervention using the Five Rights model, implements it in the EHR, then evaluates impact, monitors ongoing performance, and updates or retires it under institutional governance.
source_reference: PRIMARY: Petersen et al., 'Recommendations for the safe, effective use of adaptive CDS in the US healthcare system', AMIA position paper, JAMIA 2021;28(4):677-684, doi 10.1093/jamia/ocaa319, full text fetched at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7973467/ - documents the complete CDS lifecycle stages (design and development, implementation, evaluation, ongoing monitoring and maintenance) with transparency metrics, assurance cases, performance indicators, institutional review groups, and workforce education. SUPPORTING: eCQI Resource Center CDS page (https://ecqi.healthit.gov/cds, fetched) - CMS definition of CDS, the CDS Five Rights model (right information, people, format, channel, time) from Improving Outcomes with Clinical Decision Support, and the note that CDS impact may be assessed with an eCQM.
expert_raw_materials: Care-gap and quality reports, alert-override and alert-fatigue logs, patient-safety event reports, clinical practice guidelines, order-set and documentation-template drafts, EHR CDS knowledge artifacts, eCQM results for impact assessment.
usage_permissions: EHR production data are used under institutional policies and role-based access; guideline content is incorporated under publisher terms; CDS knowledge artifacts are governed by the institutional CDS governance committee.
task_input: CDS request from a clinical service or a detected care gap or alerting problem, with supporting guideline evidence and baseline workflow data.
professional_operations: Review the care gap or safety event and the evidence base; convene multidisciplinary review (clinicians, informatics, IT, quality); select the intervention format using the CDS Five Rights model; author or configure the rule in EHR tooling; test against representative and edge cases; implement with clinician education and change management; evaluate impact with an outcome or eCQM measure; monitor performance indicators continuously (alert override rates, drift); update or retire the intervention through the CDS governance committee.
expected_deliverable: Configured, tested, go-live CDS intervention with approval documentation, education record, and a monitoring or evaluation plan.
success_criteria: Improved process or outcome measure without new safety events; reduced alert overrides or documented rationale; scheduled governance review performed on time.
verification_approach: Override-rate and performance dashboards; eCQM or outcome measurement; chart audit of false-positive alerts; recurring CDS committee review of monitoring reports against baseline (PDSA-style comparison).
platform_dependencies: EHR CDS authoring environment (vendor or FHIR/CDS Hooks), analytics data warehouse, test patient or synthetic record sets, governance committee infrastructure.
blocking_risks: CDS configuration lives inside proprietary EHR vendor systems (institutional infrastructure, not portable software); alert-fatigue consequences of poorly tuned rules; regulatory uncertainty for self-developed adaptive CDS as documented by AMIA in the primary source.
expert_capability: Clinical informatics: workflow and knowledge management, CDS design and evaluation methods, clinical governance, EHR build competence.
cross_domain_overlap: Shares the evaluation step with med_inform_wf02 (eCQM lifecycle measures impact) - distinct because CDS changes clinician behavior while eCQM builds the measuring instrument. Adjacent to clinical_diagnostics and therapeutic_oncology workflows from the med_a round, which consume CDS rather than building it.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded, recurring institutional workflow (per CDS request), not a career and not a single rule edit.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps; combination of the AMIA lifecycle paper and the eCQI Five Rights page assembled the full chain. Optional: confirm with an AMIA CDS working-group member that the adaptive-CDS lifecycle recommendations generalize to governance of non-adaptive CDS.
data_usage_authorization: EHR production data used for CDS design and monitoring under institutional data governance; analytics extracts follow De-identified and limited data sets are governed by 45 CFR 164.514: expert determination or Safe Harbor de-identification (removal of the 18 identifier types), limited data sets require a data use agreement, and minimum-necessary limits apply to uses and disclosures (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
privacy_considerations: Patient-level extracts are identifiable EHR data protected in the US by the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); EU/UK processing is governed by GDPR and UK GDPR, so jurisdiction-specific review is required.
research_ethics: Secondary research use of patient data requires IRB or comparable ethics review; approval criteria cover risk minimization, equitable subject selection, informed consent or an approved waiver, and privacy protection per 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); the research-versus-quality-improvement determination follows the 45 CFR 46.102 definitions (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102).
reproducibility_assessment: The AMIA paper standardizes lifecycle artifacts (transparency metrics, assurance case, performance indicators cited at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7973467/), so the process is auditable; intervention outcomes remain review-dependent and the EHR rule logic is the main black-box element.
primary_claim: The AMIA position paper documents the complete CDS lifecycle: design and development with training-data transparency metrics, implementation and evaluation with an assurance case of clinical utility, deployment challenges and performance indicators, ongoing monitoring and maintenance including algorithm drift or shift review and periodic re-evaluation, institutional review-group governance, and workforce education; the eCQI Resource Center page adds the CDS Five Rights selection model and CMS definition of CDS.

workflow_title: Electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) lifecycle development: conceptualization, specification, testing, and program implementation
occupation_scope: eCQM measure analyst or developer; Clinical quality measure steward; Clinical informaticist
workflow_summary: A measure developer moves an eCQM through the CMS Measures Management System lifecycle: environmental scan and business case, CQL and HQMF specification with value sets, reliability and validity testing, rulemaking and consensus endorsement, then annual maintenance and 3-year comprehensive re-evaluation.
source_reference: PRIMARY: eCQI Resource Center eCQM Lifecycle page (https://ecqi.healthit.gov/ecqm-lifecycle, fetched 2026-11) - documents all five lifecycle stages with steps, tools, and actors: conceptualization (environmental scan, evidence base, business case), specification (CQL, HQMF, QDM, VSAC value sets), testing (scientific acceptability, feasibility, usability), implementation (rulemaking, CBE endorsement, CHPL-certified health IT), and use or maintenance (annual update, comprehensive re-evaluation every 3 years). SUPPORTING: CMS Measures Management System Blueprint (https://mmshub.cms.gov/blueprint-measure-lifecycle-overview, cited directly by the fetched page) outlining the core processes eCQM developers follow.
expert_raw_materials: Clinical guideline evidence, administrative claims and EHR data for testing, value sets from VSAC, CQL and HQMF drafts, BPS test packages, Cypress test results, business case documents.
usage_permissions: VSAC value sets are distributed under NLM UMLS Metathesaurus license terms (a UMLS license is required for download); published eCQM specifications are used for CMS program reporting under program rules.
task_input: Measure concept from a Call for Measures, stakeholder need, or measurement gap, plus supporting clinical evidence.
professional_operations: Perform environmental scan and evidence review, draft the business case; specify the measure in CQL and HQMF with QDM/QI-Core data elements and VSAC value sets; run iterative testing for reliability, validity, feasibility, and usability including health IT calculation testing (Cypress, BPS, synthetic data); submit through rulemaking and CMS consensus-based entity endorsement; publish annual updates and re-evaluate comprehensively every 3 years with stakeholder feedback.
expected_deliverable: A tested, endorsed eCQM package (logic, value sets, test outcomes, business case) adopted by a CMS quality program and implemented in certified health IT.
success_criteria: Measure passes reliability, validity, feasibility, and usability testing; certified health IT products calculate consistent rates; measure is adopted in program rulemaking and maintained on schedule.
verification_approach: Independent calculation testing in Cypress against BPS test data with expected values; public comment and Technical Expert Panel review; CBE endorsement review; certification testing of vendor implementations via ONC-ACBs.
platform_dependencies: VSAC value set repository, MADiE measure authoring environment, Cypress testing tool, eCQI Resource Center and MC Workspace (federal web platforms); ONC Health IT Certification program infrastructure.
blocking_risks: Official lifecycle tooling is government-hosted SaaS whose program context (rulemaking, CBE endorsement) is institutional rather than software; VSAC access needs an NLM UMLS license; certification of health IT products requires formal ONC-ACB testing.
expert_capability: Clinical quality measurement: CQL authoring, value set and terminology management (LOINC/SNOMED), program rules, measure testing methods.
cross_domain_overlap: Boundary to narrative quality improvement and to public_health surveillance measures (med_pubhealth rows) is the CMS program context and regulated reporting pipeline; the instrument-engineering nature (measure lifecycle) separates it from CDS selection (med_inform_wf01) and from population surveillance products.
granularity_check: Right granularity: one measure lifecycle is a bounded multi-month recurring project cycle, institutionalized as the CMS MMS process.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm the current MADiE tooling status and the 2026 CBE (P4QM) endorsement mechanics with the ONC eCQI Resource Center help desk.
data_usage_authorization: Measure data elements and testing data are handled under CMS quality program rules and institutional agreements; patient-level test extracts follow De-identified and limited data sets are governed by 45 CFR 164.514: expert determination or Safe Harbor de-identification (removal of the 18 identifier types), limited data sets require a data use agreement, and minimum-necessary limits apply to uses and disclosures (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
privacy_considerations: Patient-level extracts are identifiable EHR data protected in the US by the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); EU/UK processing is governed by GDPR and UK GDPR, so jurisdiction-specific review is required.
research_ethics: Secondary research use of patient data requires IRB or comparable ethics review; approval criteria cover risk minimization, equitable subject selection, informed consent or an approved waiver, and privacy protection per 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); the research-versus-quality-improvement determination follows the 45 CFR 46.102 definitions (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102).

workflow_title: Observational database study on an OMOP common data model research warehouse: ETL, cohort definition, feasibility, execution, and write-up
occupation_scope: Clinical data analyst; Clinical informaticist; Observational data scientist; Research informatician
workflow_summary: An academic medical center analyst converts source EHR or claims data to the OMOP common data model, defines and validates study cohorts, runs feasibility counts, pre-specifies a protocol and study package, executes characterization or estimation, and writes up results with data-quality and validity evidence.
source_reference: PRIMARY: The Book of OHDSI (OHDSI community, 2021, open access) fetched at https://ohdsi.github.io/TheBookOfOhdsi/ - documents the whole workflow: uniform data representation (OMOP CDM and standardized vocabularies, Ch 4-5), ETL design and quality control (Ch 6), cohort definition and validity (Ch 10), characterization (Ch 11), the seven study steps from question definition to interpretation and write-up (Ch 19), data quality (ACHILLES and DQD, Ch 15), clinical validity via PheValuator and source record review (Ch 16), and method validity (Ch 18). SUPPORTING: OHDSI network research chapter (NetworkResearch.html in the same fetched book) covering distributed network study design and execution.
expert_raw_materials: EHR source tables and local code sets, OMOP vocabulary and concept tables, ETL specification documents, cohort definitions, ACHILLES and DQD outputs, chart samples for source record review.
usage_permissions: OHDSI software is open source (Apache-2.0 or MIT) and the Book is open access; underlying patient data remain under institutional data governance and HIPAA compliance.
task_input: A research question from investigators plus access to an OMOP-mapped data source (or the task of mapping a new source).
professional_operations: Define the question and review data availability or quality (ACHILLES, DQD); run ETL design with White Rabbit, Rabbit-in-a-Hat, and Usagi code mapping with quality control; define cohorts in ATLAS (concept sets, inclusion and exit criteria) and validate phenotypes (PheValuator, source record review); run feasibility counts and diagnostics; pre-specify and finalize the protocol and study package; execute; interpret and write up with negative-control calibration evidence.
expected_deliverable: Executed study package with cohort definitions, characterization tables or effect estimates, protocol, and a written analysis with validity documentation.
success_criteria: Study reproduces across network sites; cohort positive predictive value meets target; pre-specified protocol was followed; results pass method-validity diagnostics.
verification_approach: Source record review of sampled charts; PheValuator cohort evaluation; negative and positive controls with p-value calibration; independent re-execution of the study package on a second database.
platform_dependencies: OMOP database (PostgreSQL or other RDBMS), OHDSI stack (WebAPI, ATLAS, R method packages), Broadsea or similar deployment, Linux server.
blocking_risks: Access to identified source data is governed by institutional IRB and data-use agreements; ETL quality depends on source-code mapping expertise; network study logistics need site participation agreements.
expert_capability: Clinical research informatics: OMOP mapping, cohort engineering, observational study design awareness, R or SQL data analysis.
cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps clinical_trials on real-world evidence and biostatistics on estimation methods; distinct because this workflow is informatics infrastructure and cohort engineering for observational evidence, while med_trials rows are regulated trial operations and statistical inference is excluded from this cluster.

workflow_title: Cross-enterprise clinical document sharing deployment: XDS.b affinity domain implementation, conformance testing, and operation
occupation_scope: Interoperability or interface analyst; Health information exchange engineer; Clinical informaticist
workflow_summary: An HIE or integration team stands up an IHE XDS.b affinity domain: agreeing domain policies, configuring document source, repository, registry, and consumer actors, publishing and registering clinical documents with metadata, querying and retrieving them across enterprises, and keeping audit trails under ATNA.
source_reference: PRIMARY: IHE IT Infrastructure Technical Framework Volume 1, Section 10, Cross-Enterprise Document Sharing (XDS.b), Final Text Revision 20.2, November 11 2025, fetched at https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/TF/Volume1/ch-10.html - documents the complete document sharing workflow: Document Source submits documents and metadata via Provide and Register Document Set-b (ITI-41), the Repository registers them with the Registry (ITI-42) with metadata validation, Consumers query via Registry Stored Query (ITI-18) and retrieve via Retrieve Document Set (ITI-43), patient identity feed (ITI-8 or 44), required groupings with Consistent Time and ATNA audit trail, affinity domain policies and metadata vocabulary, document lifecycle (approved, deprecated, replacement RPLC, addendum APND, transformation XFRM). SUPPORTING: IHE Wiki XDS page (https://wiki.ihe.net/index.php/Cross-Enterprise_Document_Sharing, fetched) linking the formal specification and companion profiles (PIX, PDQ, XCA, ATNA).
expert_raw_materials: Affinity domain policy documents, local document type and metadata code sets (LOINC document codes), patient identity domain assignments, transaction test scripts, ATNA audit records, conformance test results.
usage_permissions: IHE Technical Framework texts and profiles are published by IHE International for implementation; patient document exchange is governed by affinity domain policies covering consent, patient identification, and access control.
task_input: Need for interoperable document exchange between healthcare enterprises plus agreement of an affinity domain to share records.
professional_operations: Define affinity domain policies (document formats, metadata value sets, patient identification domain); configure and group the actors (document source and repository, registry, consumer; consistent time and ATNA secure node); publish documents with submission sets and metadata; register with metadata validation by the registry; query and retrieve documents for care; manage the document lifecycle (replacement, addendum, deprecation); conformance-test transactions and audit the trail.
expected_deliverable: Operating XDS.b affinity domain with registry and repositories, conformant member connections, and required ATNA audit trail.
success_criteria: Cross-enterprise query returns valid, retrievable document entries; all transactions pass conformance testing; audit trail satisfies ATNA requirements.
verification_approach: IHE Connectathon and Gazelle conformance testing of each actor; end-to-end query and retrieve testing with a partner enterprise; ATNA audit log review; metadata validation checks by the registry.
platform_dependencies: XDS.b registry and repository infrastructure, web-service stacks (ebXML SOAP), ATNA and consistent time services, per-domain policies.
blocking_risks: Affinity domain policy agreements (consent and patient ID) are organizational, not software; production HIE deployments often use proprietary gateways; certificate and identity management are required for secure operation.
expert_capability: Health informatics interoperability: IHE profile semantics, ebXML message structure, terminology and metadata mapping, security and audit configuration.
cross_domain_overlap: Shares the standards layer with med_inform_wf02's ONC certification ecosystem but transports documents instead of measure logic; complemented by patient matching (PIX/PDQ) profiles; distinct from care-delivery workflows that consume exchanged documents.
granularity_check: Right granularity: affinity domain implementation is a bounded system-delivery workflow with a recurring conformance-testing cycle, not a single integration edit.

privacy_considerations: Patient-level extracts are identifiable EHR data protected in the US by the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); EU/UK processing is governed by GDPR and UK GDPR, so jurisdiction-specific review is required.

workflow_title: Notifiable disease case surveillance: mandatory case reporting, case investigation, and national case notification through NNDSS
occupation_scope: Public health surveillance officer; Health department epidemiologist; Public health informatician
workflow_summary: Jurisdictional health departments receive legally mandated reports of diagnosed reportable conditions from providers, hospitals, and laboratories (via eCR and ELR), conduct case investigations to collect clinical and epidemiologic details and initiate control actions, then send de-identified case notifications for national notifiable conditions to CDC NNDSS, which validates, processes, and provisions the data to national disease programs.
source_reference: PRIMARY: CDC NNDSS (https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/conducting.html, fetched): documents the two-component case surveillance process - mandatory case reporting steps (diagnosis/confirmation reported to the health department; health department uses data for outbreak control, treatment assurance, and preventive care for exposed persons) and voluntary case notification steps (de-identified data sent to CDC; the NNDSS team receives, secures, processes, and provides data to disease-specific CDC programs), plus the methods eCR, ELR, NEDSS/NBS investigation-workflow systems, METS message validation, and MVPS validation/processing; SUPPORTING: CDC (https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/index.html, fetched): reportable-vs-notifiable distinction, about 120 notifiable conditions, about 3,000 health departments and 2.7M cases/year, CSTE and CDC set the national list, and CDC notification case records contain no personally identifiable information; CSTE/CDC case definitions repository (https://ndc.services.cdc.gov/, cited by the fetched CDC Field Epidemiology Manual chapter at https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html).
expert_raw_materials: eCR and ELR messages; jurisdictional surveillance system records (NEDSS Base System or compatible); CSTE/CDC condition-specific case definitions; case investigation forms, interview notes, and laboratory results; state reportable-condition schedules and the annual NNDSS notifiable list; HL7 case notification messages validated through METS.
usage_permissions: Surveillance records are held and worked under state/local public health legal authority; national case notifications are de-identified and centrally provisioned by CDC NNDSS; CSTE/CDC case definitions are public documents in the ndc.services.cdc.gov repository; METS and MVPS services are restricted to jurisdictional users.
task_input: Reportable-condition reports (eCR/ELR) and lab/clinical results; the applicable CSTE/CDC case definition; the jurisdiction's reportable-condition list and investigation procedures.
professional_operations: Receive and triage eCR/ELR and provider reports against the case definition; open an investigation record in the jurisdictional system; collect demographic, clinical, epidemiologic, and exposure details; classify the case per case-definition criteria; initiate control actions (treatment follow-up, contact notification, prophylaxis, source control); validate and transmit de-identified notification for notifiable conditions to CDC via METS/MVPS; respond to CDC program queries and maintain data quality.
expected_deliverable: Completed case investigation records; de-identified case notifications submitted to NNDSS; documented disease-control actions; ad hoc jurisdictional reports and data extracts.
success_criteria: Complete, timely notifications accepted by MVPS; case classification matching CSTE/CDC case definition criteria; control actions initiated per protocol; no backlog of unprocessed reports.
verification_approach: METS message validation before transmission; MVPS portal data-quality review by jurisdictions; audit against case definition criteria; peer review within the health department program.
platform_dependencies: Jurisdictional surveillance information system (NEDSS Base System or NEDSS-compatible), eCR/EHR and ELR interfaces, METS and MVPS (CDC-hosted services), HL7 messaging, ndc.services.cdc.gov case definition repository.
blocking_risks: The workflow runs inside institutional public health systems (jurisdictional surveillance systems and CDC-hosted message services) with no portable equivalent; state-law variation in reporting requirements; identifiable case data cannot leave jurisdictional control, so automation must be embedded in health department environments; eCR/MMG onboarding requires CDC coordination.
expert_capability: Applied epidemiology with disease-specific investigation protocols, public health informatics (HL7/eCR/MMG message mapping), and command of state reporting laws and case definitions.
cross_domain_overlap: Feeds med_pubhealth_wf02 (outbreak investigations draw on case-level line listings) - distinct because wf01 is the routine case-level reporting-to-notification supply chain and wf02 is the episodic field response; touches clinical_informatics via eCR/EHR interfaces - distinct because clinical_informatics builds and operates the sending EHR systems while public health operates the receiving surveillance workflow.
granularity_check: Correct granularity: a bounded recurring per-case/per-batch workflow, not a career and not a single micro-action.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm current MMG onboarding and eCR readiness thresholds with the NNDSS onboarding team (edx@cdc.gov).
data_usage_authorization: Case reporting by providers, hospitals, and laboratories is mandatory under state and local disease-reporting laws; notification to CDC is voluntary under CSTE/CDC agreements and CDC notification records contain no personally identifiable information (CDC NNDSS: https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/index.html). Case-level identifiable data remain under state/local health department legal authority; CDC processing is federal public health surveillance authority.
privacy_considerations: Case-level records are personally identifiable at the jurisdictional level and are protected under state disease-reporting laws; CDC notification records are de-identified (https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/index.html). US federal de-identification benchmarks for any shared analytic extracts follow the HIPAA Safe Harbor or expert determination standards of 45 CFR 164.514 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
research_ethics: Routine disease surveillance and outbreak control are public health practice under legal authority rather than human-subjects research; where an investigation adds systematic data collection or analytic studies intended for publication, the Common Rule research determination and IRB approval criteria in 45 CFR 46.111 apply (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111). Under 45 CFR 46.102(l)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102), public health surveillance activities conducted, supported, or authorized by a public health authority and limited to identifying, monitoring, and investigating public health signals, outbreaks, and conditions of public health importance - including mandatory case reporting and voluntary NNDSS notification - are deemed not to be research for purposes of the Common Rule.
reproducibility_assessment: The workflow is standardized through public CSTE/CDC case definitions (ndc.services.cdc.gov, cited by the fetched https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html), fixed reporting chains (eCR/ELR to jurisdiction, jurisdiction to CDC), and message-level validation (METS) plus MVPS processing (https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/conducting.html); jurisdiction-specific investigative practice and state-law variation are the less standardized parts.
primary_claim: CDC documents the complete national case surveillance workflow: mandatory case reporting by providers, hospitals, and laboratories to health departments, health department investigation and disease-control actions, and voluntary de-identified case notification to CDC through NNDSS with validation (METS), processing (MVPS), and provisioning to CDC programs, supported by eCR, ELR, and NEDSS-base systems.

workflow_title: Epidemiologic field investigation of an outbreak (CDC 10-step method: confirm, characterize, control, communicate)
workflow_summary: After official authorization, a public health team confirms the diagnosis, verifies that an outbreak exists against expected baselines, builds a case definition and line listing, characterizes cases in time, place, and person, considers immediate control measures, develops and tests hypotheses, plans systematic studies, implements and evaluates control and prevention measures, and communicates findings through briefings and written reports.
source_reference: PRIMARY: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual, Ch. 3 Conducting a Field Investigation (King, Bensyl, Goodman, Rasmussen; https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html, fetched): documents the complete 10-step field investigation workflow, including the three-element case definition (condition, period, setting), line listing, epidemic-curve construction at one-fourth to one-third of the incubation period, spot maps and denominators, source-directed versus susceptible-directed control measures, hypothesis testing with cohort/case-control studies and Bradford Hill considerations, active surveillance to evaluate control measures, and the communications plan ending in a preliminary written report and oral briefing to the requesting authority before leaving the field, with MMWR brief reports for rapid dissemination; discussion includes state legal privacy obligations for case information; SUPPORTING: CDC NNDSS case definitions repository (https://ndc.services.cdc.gov/, cited directly by this chapter) for the standard case definitions used in counting cases.
expert_raw_materials: Line listings; structured questionnaires (e.g., the CDC National Hypothesis Generating Questionnaire); laboratory results and strain typing; medical and institutional records; denominator counts (e.g., total event attendees); surveillance baselines; epidemic curves, spot maps, and other descriptive graphics; communications plans and briefing materials.
usage_permissions: Investigation data are collected under state/local public health legal authority following a formal invitation from an authorized official; laboratory work is coordinated with designated laboratories; questionnaire and case-definition tools are standard CDC instruments.
task_input: Notification of a suspected outbreak or cluster plus a formal invitation/authorization from the requesting authority.
professional_operations: 1 Prepare for field work (authorization, roles, laboratory coordination, PPE); 2 Confirm the diagnosis (interviews, exams, records, lab results; rule out pseudoepidemics); 3 Determine the existence of an outbreak (compare observed with expected counts/rates over a comparator timeframe); 4 Identify and count cases (case definition, active case finding, line listing); 5 Tabulate and orient data by time, place, and person (epidemic curves, spot maps, denominators); 6 Consider whether control measures can be implemented now; 7 Develop and test hypotheses (structured interviews, analytic studies, Bradford Hill considerations); 8 Plan one or more systematic studies; 9 Implement and evaluate control and prevention measures with concurrent active surveillance; 10 Communicate findings (communications plan, designated spokesperson, preliminary written report and oral briefing, final report, brief report for MMWR-type bulletins).
expected_deliverable: Line listing and descriptive epidemiologic products; preliminary written report and oral briefing to the requesting authority; recommendations for control; evaluation of control measures; final written report and possibly a brief report for a public health bulletin.
success_criteria: Outbreak confirmed or refuted on documented evidence; control measures implemented and shown by active surveillance to reduce or stop new cases; requesting authority receives the preliminary report and briefing before the team leaves the field.
verification_approach: Peer review by state/national colleagues; comparison of post-control case incidence via active surveillance; verification of case counts against laboratory results; requesting-authority review of the written report.
platform_dependencies: Line-listing and statistical software (spreadsheets, R or equivalent), mapping/GIS or simple plotting tools, laboratory information channels, secure communication for PII, and no specialized hardware.
blocking_risks: Substantial parts are inherently field-person work (interviews, site visits, briefings) that software cannot perform; access to identifiable case and exposure data is restricted by state law; laboratory confirmation and institutional EHR access depend on partnerships; readiness depends on trained field epidemiology staff.
expert_capability: Applied field epidemiology capability as taught in CDC EIS courses: descriptive and analytic epidemiology under time pressure, case-definition judgment, and public health communication.
cross_domain_overlap: Relies on case identification from med_pubhealth_wf01 (routine case surveillance builds the baseline and initial line listing) - distinct because wf01 is the routine case-level supply chain and wf02 is the episodic acute response; analytic study design within investigations is adjacent to clinical_trials observational study work - distinct because this is an urgent public health response under health authority, not regulated clinical research.
granularity_check: Correct granularity: an episodic but recurring, bounded professional workflow with published steps, not a career or micro-action.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm current practice details (case-definition revision and control-measure timing) with a jurisdiction's state epidemiologist.
data_usage_authorization: Field investigation data collection operates under state/local public health legal authority, with a formal invitation from an authorized official required before assistance begins (https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html); reported case data flow through the mandatory state-level reporting system documented by CDC NNDSS (https://www.cdc.gov/nndss/what-is-case-surveillance/index.html).
privacy_considerations: Investigation line listings contain personally identifiable information; the manual directs investigators to know applicable local, state, and federal privacy laws when collecting information from affected persons and their contacts (https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html); US de-identification benchmarks follow 45 CFR 164.514 Safe Harbor or expert determination (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
research_ethics: Outbreak response is public health practice under legal authority, generally distinct from research; any systematic data collection or study added for publication in an investigation falls under the Common Rule research determination and IRB criteria of 45 CFR 46.111, including privacy safeguards and risk minimization (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111). Under 45 CFR 46.102(l)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102), public health surveillance activities conducted by a public health authority - including outbreak field investigations - are deemed not to be research when limited to detecting, monitoring, and investigating public health signals, outbreaks, and conditions of public health importance.
reproducibility_assessment: The CDC chapter enumerates reproducible elements: case definition structure, line-listing fields, epidemic-curve interval rules, and reporting products, enabling SOP-based replication (https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/field-investigation.html); judgment calls such as case-definition revision and control-measure timing remain expert-dependent parts of the workflow.
primary_claim: The CDC Field Epidemiology Manual documents the complete 10-step outbreak field investigation: preparation with official authorization; diagnosis confirmation; outbreak verification against baseline; case definition and line-listing case finding; time/place/person characterization with epidemic curves and spot maps; timely control measures; hypothesis development and testing; systematic studies; implementation and evaluation of control measures; and communication through briefings and written reports.

workflow_title: Daily syndromic surveillance monitoring and aberration investigation on the NSSP BioSense Platform (ESSENCE)
occupation_scope: Syndromic surveillance analyst; Health department epidemiologist
workflow_summary: Jurisdictional analysts access the NSSP BioSense Platform daily, review near real-time de-identified emergency department data (chief complaints, diagnosis codes, patient characteristics, location) for counts above expected baselines, run syndrome queries in the ESSENCE tool, investigate signals for outbreak plausibility, and communicate or escalate actionable findings - an early warning layer that precedes confirmed-disease reporting.
source_reference: PRIMARY: CDC NSSP About (For Public Health) (https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/index.html, fetched): documents the syndromic surveillance operation - de-identified facility data including chief complaint, diagnosis codes, patient characteristics, and location flow through health departments/HIEs into the CDC-hosted BioSense Platform where public health practitioners conduct surveillance activities to detect unusual levels of illness and determine whether a response is needed; lists integrated data sources (ED data, laboratory, mortality, DoD/VA, weather, air quality) and scale (7,500+ facilities, 85% of US EDs, 10.2M messages/day, data within 24 hours); SUPPORTING: CDC Syndromic Surveillance for New Users (https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/how-we-conduct-syndromic-surveillance.html, fetched): platform access is governed by jurisdictional site administrators, and ESSENCE is defined as the secure web-based tool that operationalizes the public health surveillance workflow, allowing analysts to collaborate, investigate changes in trends, and analyze, visualize, and share data; CDC MMWR overview of syndromic surveillance (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/su5301a3.htm, fetched): aberration-detection methods compare day-to-day and day-and-place variability against an expected baseline, response protocols need documented procedures and staff, diagnostic confirmation is a paramount alert-investigation step, and (as of 2004) signal-detection methods were not yet standardized.
expert_raw_materials: ED chief-complaint free text and coded fields; diagnosis codes; patient demographic and location fields; daily syndrome counts; ESSENCE queries, dashboards, and alert settings; data quality reports; baseline thresholds adjusted for seasonality and facility participation.
usage_permissions: BioSense Platform accounts are issued through jurisdictional site administrators who review data-access requests; platform data are de-identified; NSSP Community of Practice and knowledge repository resources support authorized users.
task_input: Daily refreshed BioSense Platform data plus situational requests (mass gatherings, disasters, respiratory season monitoring).
professional_operations: Maintain platform access through the site administrator; define categorical syndrome subsets and query library for the jurisdiction; review dashboards and alerts on a daily schedule; run ESSENCE queries against expected baselines to detect aberrations; investigate signals (clustering by location, severe symptoms, unexplained deaths, simultaneous multi-source alerts); pursue diagnostic confirmation where possible; document dispositions and communicate or escalate findings to investigation teams, and adjust syndrome definitions as disease knowledge evolves.
expected_deliverable: Daily situational awareness products; investigated and dispositioned alert records; event-related syndromic summaries; periodic reports of trends; documentation of syndrome definitions used.
success_criteria: Aberrations are detected in near real-time (data within 24 hours of visits); alerts are triaged and dispositioned with documented rationale; detected signals contribute to earlier investigation or response; monitoring continuity documented across analysts.
verification_approach: Corroboration of signals with other data sources (case reports, laboratories); diagnostic confirmation as part of alert investigation (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/su5301a3.htm); data quality review via platform reports; community of practice peer review of queries and definitions.
platform_dependencies: NSSP BioSense Platform (CDC-hosted cloud system) and the ESSENCE web application; jurisdictional data feed arrangements through health departments or HIEs; site-administrator account governance.
blocking_risks: The platform and ESSENCE are government-hosted services with jurisdiction-governed access and no self-host path, so the workflow cannot be reproduced outside official access; low positive predictive value of individual signals places the analytic burden on trained staff; alert thresholds remain jurisdiction-tuned rather than standardized; free-text coding quality varies by facility.
expert_capability: Syndromic surveillance methods training (e.g., CSTE introductory methodology courses linked from https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/how-we-conduct-syndromic-surveillance.html), time-series/aberration-detection literacy, and disease-epidemiology judgment.
cross_domain_overlap: Complements med_pubhealth_wf01 (case-based surveillance) and med_pubhealth_wf02 (outbreak investigation triggered by signals) - distinct because detection uses pre-diagnostic ED data in near real-time rather than confirmed case reports and laboratory follow-up; adjacent to clinical_informatics data feeds - distinct because informatics operates the sending EHR/eCR systems and public health operates the detection workflow.
granularity_check: Correct granularity: a bounded recurring daily workflow owned by a defined analyst role, not a career or micro-action.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm current daily-monitoring SOP specifics (alert review cadence and disposition standards) with the NSSP CoP/OPHDST (nssp@cdc.gov).
data_usage_authorization: NSSP operates as a federal-state data-sharing program: participating facilities send de-identified syndromic data to state/local health departments and HIEs, which contribute to the CDC-hosted BioSense Platform for authorized public health surveillance (https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/index.html), and platform access is granted through jurisdictional site administrators (https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/how-we-conduct-syndromic-surveillance.html).
privacy_considerations: Syndromic records are de-identified before submission to health departments and the BioSense Platform per the NSSP data flow (https://www.cdc.gov/nssp/php/about/index.html); small-count disclosures still require statistical disclosure control, and the US de-identification benchmark is 45 CFR 164.514 Safe Harbor or expert determination (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
research_ethics: Syndromic surveillance is public health practice; the MMWR overview stresses that it does not replace traditional surveillance or physician reporting of unusual cases (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/su5301a3.htm); any research use of platform data follows the Common Rule research determination and IRB criteria of 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111). Under 45 CFR 46.102(l)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102), public health surveillance conducted or authorized by a public health authority - including syndromic surveillance - is deemed not to be research when limited to detecting, monitoring, and investigating public health signals, outbreaks, and conditions of public health importance.
reproducibility_assessment: Platform-level tools and training make day-to-day query and visualization practice reproducible, but the MMWR overview documents that signal-detection methods and response protocols were historically not standardized across jurisdictions (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/su5301a3.htm), so alert thresholds and syndrome definitions remain jurisdiction-specific rather than a single auditable standard.
primary_claim: CDC documents the NSSP syndromic surveillance operation: facilities send de-identified emergency-department data (chief complaint, diagnosis codes, patient characteristics, location) to health departments and HIEs, which contribute to the BioSense Platform where public health practitioners monitor near real-time data to detect unusual levels of illness and determine whether a response is needed.

workflow_title: BRFSS annual prevalence estimation: weighted analysis of the complex-survey public-use data file
occupation_scope: Public health data analyst; Health department epidemiologist (BRFSS coordinator)
workflow_summary: Each year, public health analysts obtain the BRFSS combined landline/cell public-use file, prepare variables with the codebook and calculated-variable documentation, apply the raked complex-sampling weights to the survey design, and compute state-level prevalence estimates of health risk behaviors with design-based variance estimation for reports, policy monitoring, and comparisons across post-2011 years.
source_reference: PRIMARY: CDC 2024 BRFSS Survey Data and Documentation (https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_2024.html, fetched): documents the annual data-release workflow - the combined landline and cell phone dataset (457,670 records; 49 states plus DC, Guam, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands), raking weighting methodology in place since 2011 with the cell-phone frame, the codebook, calculated-variables documentation, variable layout, weighting/format resources, and the data quality report with response rates; states no data are not comparable to pre-2011 years; notes 2024 files were modified to comply with executive orders with possible missing-value inconsistencies; SUPPORTING: Complex Sampling Weights and Preparing Module Data for Analysis guidance (2024, https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/2024/pdf/Complex-Sampling-Weights-and-Preparing-Module-Data-for-Analysis-2024-508.pdf - cited by the primary page; PDF not parsed in this round - the primary page records that it explains the need for complex sampling weights and instructions for preparing a module data set for analysis).
expert_raw_materials: BRFSS LLCP ASCII or SAS-transport public-use file; annual codebook; variable layout; calculated-variable documentation; complex-sampling-weights guidance; data quality report; optional module data files.
usage_permissions: Public-use data files and documentation are freely downloadable for analysis; respondent-level identifying data remain with state survey operations; the public-use files are de-identified.
task_input: BRFSS annual public-use data plus an analytic request (target indicators, geographic units, and population subgroups).
professional_operations: Download the data file, codebook, and variable layout; read and validate the fixed-position data; map variables and recode to analytic measures; build derived/calculated variables per documentation; declare the complex survey design with the raked weight (_LLCPWT) and strata; compute weighted prevalence and design-based confidence intervals for target indicators and subgroups; apply post-2011 comparability rules when trending across years; produce tables, maps, and reports with a methodology note.
expected_deliverable: Weighted prevalence estimates and design-based confidence intervals in tabular/report form; methodology documentation; monitoring briefs or public dashboards for health policy audiences.
success_criteria: Estimates reproduce CDC published BRFSS prevalence tables within rounding; standard errors reflect the complex design; trend statements respect the pre-2011 comparability boundary documented by CDC.
verification_approach: Replication against CDC published annual prevalence tables; data quality report review (response rates, coverage); state BRFSS coordinator review; independent code review of the weighting and recode logic.
platform_dependencies: Statistical software supporting complex survey designs (R survey package, SAS/SUDAAN, or Stata) on any OS; the ASCII/XPT public-use formats import on Linux through open packages; no proprietary runtime is strictly required.
blocking_risks: The 2024 weighting-formula detail is published as PDF documentation that must be read carefully to replicate CDC weights; executive-order-driven 2024 data modifications create missing-value inconsistencies noted by CDC; misuse of weights (unweighted analysis, ignoring design effects) silently invalidates estimates, so analyst training is the main gate.
expert_capability: Complex-survey statistics (design-based estimation, raking/calibration understanding) plus behavioral-health indicator domain knowledge.
cross_domain_overlap: Adjacent to med_pubhealth_wf01 (surveillance) - distinct because this is population-survey statistical analysis of a cross-sectional probability sample rather than communicable case data operations; methodologically adjacent to med_inform_wf03 (observational OMOP studies) - distinct because BRFSS is design-weighted survey estimation while OHDSI is EHR cohort analytics; design-based survey estimation sits at the applied-epidemiology edge of biostatistics.
granularity_check: Correct granularity: a bounded recurring annual workflow with fixed CDC documentation and a defined analyst role, not a career or micro-action.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm current weighting-formula implementation details with the BRFSS methodology team or a state BRFSS coordinator (the annual weighting PDF was not parsed in this round).
data_usage_authorization: BRFSS is a federally supported, state-implemented public health survey; CDC releases de-identified public-use annual data and documentation for analysis (https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_2024.html), and state survey operations run under CDC cooperative-agreement funding (BRFSS NOFO linked from the same page).
privacy_considerations: BRFSS public-use files contain de-identified respondent records released by CDC (https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_2024.html); analysts must not attempt re-identification, and US de-identification benchmarks follow 45 CFR 164.514 Safe Harbor or expert determination (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514).
research_ethics: BRFSS data collection is public health surveillance activity; secondary research analyses of the public-use files follow the Common Rule research determination and IRB criteria of 45 CFR 46.111, including risk minimization and privacy safeguards (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111). Under 45 CFR 46.102(l)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102), public health surveillance activities supported by a public health authority - including the CDC-supported, state-conducted BRFSS - are deemed not to be research when limited to identifying, monitoring, and investigating conditions of public health importance.
reproducibility_assessment: The analysis pipeline is codified in annual CDC documentation: fixed-width/variable layout, codebook, calculated-variable definitions, and the complex-sampling-weights guidance for preparing module data (https://www.cdc.gov/brfss/annual_data/annual_2024.html), so identical software and file versions reproduce identical estimates; analyst recoding choices are the remaining less standardized part.
primary_claim: CDC's 2024 BRFSS data and documentation page establishes the annual prevalence-estimation workflow: a public-use combined landline/cell file (457,670 records from 49 states plus DC, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the US Virgin Islands) analyzed with raked complex-sampling weights (raking in place since 2011), supported by the codebook, variable layout, calculated-variable documentation, module-data weighting guidance, and a data-quality report, with pre-2011 years not comparable.

workflow_title: Clinical trial site monitoring visits with source data verification (SDV)
occupation_scope: Clinical research associate (CRA) / clinical monitor; sponsor clinical operations and GCP quality assurance staff
workflow_summary: The sponsor's clinical monitor visits investigational sites on a planned schedule to verify that the study proceeds per protocol, GCP, and applicable regulations, compares source documents against case report form data (SDV), manages findings and queries, and documents the whole trail in monitoring reports from initiation through site close-out.
source_reference: PRIMARY: 21 CFR 312.56, Review of ongoing investigations (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/312.56, fetched/read): the sponsor SHALL monitor the progress of all clinical investigations under its IND, secure compliance or discontinue an investigator on discovering noncompliance, and act on unreasonable and significant risk within 5 working days. SUPPORTING: 21 CFR 312.50, General responsibilities of sponsors (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/312.50, fetched/read): sponsor duties include ensuring proper monitoring of the investigation; FDA guidance 'Electronic Source Data in Clinical Investigations' (Sept 2013, docket FDA-2010-D-0643, https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/electronic-source-data-clinical-investigations, fetched/read): authorized source data originators, data element identifiers that facilitate audit-trail examination, and manual or electronic capture of source data into the eCRF - the objects SDV inspects; FDA guidance 'A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring' (Aug 2013, docket FDA-2011-D-0597, https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/oversight-clinical-investigations-risk-based-approach-monitoring, fetched/read): monitoring as sponsor oversight focused on critical data and processes; GCDMP chapter 'Electronic Data Capture - Study Conduct, Maintenance and Closeout' (https://www.jscdm.org/article/id/31/, fetched/read, doi 10.47912/jscdm.31): quotes ICH E6(R2) sections 5.0/5.5 on sponsor oversight and source data, and records that SDV backlogs erode EDC value. The full ICH E6(R3) text was not HTML-accessible at research time (ich.org/EMA blocked), so its monitoring sections are cited only as referenced by fetched pages.
expert_raw_materials: Trial master file (TMF): monitoring plan, Form FDA-1572, delegation of authority log, IRB/IEC approvals; source documents (paper or electronic medical charts, lab reports, signed informed-consent forms); eCRF/EDC records with audit trails; monitoring visit logs and reports; correspondence with investigator; drug/device accountability records; SAE reconciliation lists
usage_permissions: Monitoring is a sponsor duty under 21 CFR 312.50 and 312.56 exercised per the study monitoring plan; site access to identifiable records requires site/IRB authorization and HIPAA-compliant disclosure basis (45 CFR 164.512(i) individual authorization or IRB waiver); monitors act under confidentiality agreements; TMF access governed by sponsor document-management permissions
task_input: Activated site: qualified investigator, executed 1572, IRB-approved protocol and amendments, enrolled subjects with eCRF data and source records, monitoring plan with visit schedule, safety and drug-accountability records
professional_operations: 1) Pre-study assessment and site selection; 2) site initiation visit (training, IRB approval verification, supplies, facility checks); 3) follow the monitoring calendar through interim monitoring visits; 4) verify signed informed consent exists for each enrolled subject and protocol compliance; 5) source data verification against eCRF for accuracy and completeness; 6) drug/device accountability and safety-reporting checks; 7) record findings, open queries and corrective actions with due dates; 8) write the monitoring visit report and escalate per risk thresholds; 9) close-out visit (finding resolution, archiving completeness, drug return, records retention)
expected_deliverable: Monitoring visit reports filed in the TMF; resolved queries with documented deviations; corrective and preventive action records; reconciled safety and drug-accountability logs; site close-out report
success_criteria: No unresolved critical findings at database lock; SDV coverage meets the monitoring plan; query resolution before lock per med_trials_wf02 gates; visit reports filed on schedule; protocol-deviation trends within acceptable limits across sites
verification_approach: Sponsor GCP quality assurance audits sample TMF/monitoring reports against SOPs; FDA BIMO inspections (21 CFR 312.68) review the same trail; CRO/sponsor monitoring management reviews reports per SOP; database-lock data-cleaning reports confirm query resolution
platform_dependencies: CTMS for visit scheduling and reporting; validated EDC with audit trail (21 CFR Part 11); eTMF/document management; electronic source access or remote monitoring tooling where EMRs are electronic; institutional site credentials; travel logistics
blocking_risks: Site access is governed by health-system policies, IRBs, and consent - an external agent cannot self-provision; SDV against heterogeneous EMR systems without standard APIs; CTMS/eTMF/EDC suites are commercial SaaS (portions replaceable by open EDC/CTMS such as OpenClinica but re-validation is costly); ICH E6(R3) procedural text is PDF-only on blocked hosts
expert_capability: GCP-credentialed CRA: protocol and regulatory fluency, source-data verification technique, risk escalation judgment, site training and corrective-action communication
cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps med_trials_wf02 (SDV-verified eCRFs feed data cleaning; distinct: wf02 owns the database to lock), med_trials_wf04 (risk-based strategy allocates visit frequency and triggers; distinct: wf04 designs where eyes go, wf01 puts eyes on site), and general audit workflows in other domains (legal/regulatory; distinct: clinical GCP compliance); biostatistics boundary: statistical monitoring designs belong to statistics, not this workflow
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded recurring per-study/per-site operational workflow from pre-study to close-out visit, neither a career nor a micro-action
pending_confirmation: Confirm with a GCP QA lead or ACRP-certified CRA that the reconstructed visit sequence (pre-study, initiation, interim monitoring with SDV, close-out) matches ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 monitoring provisions, whose full text was not HTML-accessible at research time (EMA/ich.org blocked or PDF-only); also confirm that SDV coverage follows the sponsor's monitoring plan rather than any fixed regulatory minimum.
data_usage_authorization: Sponsor monitoring duty mandated by 21 CFR 312.56(a) and 312.50 under the IND; access to identifiable subject data at sites is authorized under HIPAA 45 CFR 164.512(i) (individual authorization or IRB waiver) with minimum-necessary limits per 45 CFR 164.514(d); electronic records inspected must meet 21 CFR Part 11 controls (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/part-11); IND records retention per 21 CFR 312.57
privacy_considerations: Monitors handle subject-identifiable records; disclosure bases are HIPAA individual authorization or an IRB-approved waiver (45 CFR 164.512(i), https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.512), with access limited to the minimum necessary (45 CFR 164.514(d), https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); non-US jurisdictions apply their own rules (e.g., EU GDPR Article 89 research derogations in member-state law)
